title: Patch, protect, and watch for weakness
subtitle: WSUS rings, a living inventory, ePO & credentialed scanning
description: Keep the proven state from drifting: Windows updates through WSUS rings fed across the air gap, one approved source per software type (with SBD-REPO01 from course 1.8 for Linux packages), a living inventory on SBD-MGMT01, managed endpoint protection through SBD-EPO01, and SBD-NESSUS01 turning the scan cadence into routine.
outcomes: Deliver Windows updates through ring-gated, air-gap-fed channels, with one approved source per software type.
Prove protection coverage against a living component inventory.
Run credentialed vulnerability scanning on the standing cadence with classified findings.

stages.title: Design the rings and the software rules
stages.detail: Decide how change reaches the network before any of it does: update rings that try things on the expendable before the essential, one approved source per software type (with SBD-REPO01 from course 1.8 already serving Linux), and register rows for every new path.

stages.title: Build SBD-WSUS01 and the ring policies
stages.detail: WSUS becomes the only road Windows updates travel: content imported across the air gap, approvals per ring, and Group Policy objects (GPOs) that point every OU at the server — with a pilot ring that proves each approval first.

stages.title: SBD-MGMT01 and the living inventory
stages.detail: The course 1.12 fleet inventory was a snapshot; SBD-MGMT01 makes it a living record — every system, its ring, its sources, its last-seen state — maintained from the management seat the model placed in VLAN 70.

stages.title: Endpoint protection through SBD-EPO01
stages.detail: Protection becomes a managed fact, not fifty local settings: the ePO server deploys agents ring by ring, policy comes from one console, and the fleet's protection state is something the dashboard can simply show.

stages.title: SBD-NESSUS01 and the standing cadence
stages.detail: The course 1.5 cadence grows its instrument: credentialed scans per VLAN on schedule, findings flowing into the pipeline and the Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) habit, and this course's four new systems getting their own baselines on the way out.

outcomeSummary: Updates by ring, software from approved sources, managed protection, and a scanner that keeps everyone honest.
